data.hypothesis: The previous valid atomic candidate averaged 7.72 µs, versus the valid baseline's 46.67 µs, but its contribution from the 2048-items-per-CTA target and 1024-CTA cap is unisolated. This contrasting configuration targets 8192 items per CTA and caps at 512 CTAs: fewer contending atomics may help the large input, while increased per-CTA work and reduced parallelism may hurt. The candidate remains unmeasured and should be checked against the baseline and hierarchical approach.

memory_lessons.applicability: Large-input reduction candidates using ordered output zeroing and CTA-local atomic aggregation.
memory_lessons.claim: The supplied atomic candidate was valid on all 10 correctness cases and measured at 7.72 µs mean; the supplied valid baseline measured at 46.67 µs. These observations do not isolate why the candidate was faster.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this lower-CTA-count, higher-work-per-CTA configuration with the same checks and repeated timing protocol.

data.notes: This proposal changes only src/candidate.cu. The previous atomic candidate's reported correctness and three timing samples are supplied observations, not results for this configuration. The controller should run all correctness checks and repeated timings before drawing a performance conclusion.
transformations: For n <= 0, asynchronously zero out on the default stream; for n >= 1<<20, launch output zeroing followed by the reduction on the same default stream.
Use 256-thread CTAs with a grid-stride accumulation, target 8192 input elements per CTA, and cap the grid at 512 CTAs; each CTA performs one int32 atomicAdd after a warp/shared-memory reduction.
Retain the existing hierarchical reduction and output copy for positive inputs below the large-input threshold.
